title: Consumer returning retry re-delivers the same message-id with an incremented attempt counter
asA: developer whose consumer needs to handle transient failures without human intervention
iWant: a consumer that returns retry to observe the same message-id on the next delivery with an incremented attempt counter
soThat: policy decisions like log at attempt 2, alert at attempt N-1 are trivially expressed in code

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given the SIMULATE_CONSUMER_RETRY=true induced-failure switch on the fixture, when the consumer returns retry on the first delivery, then the second delivery observes the same stable message-id with attempts incremented to 2; the same holds on the third delivery with attempts 3. The retry-and-dlq probe records the full trajectory 1 to 3 attempts on the same message-id.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a message published with the SIMULATE_CONSUMER_RETRY switch true on the fixture
acceptanceCriteria.when: the consumer is invoked across successive deliveries
acceptanceCriteria.then: the message-id is stable across attempts 1 to 3; the attempt counter increments on each delivery; body, headers and producer-supplied trace-id remain byte-equal across attempts

acceptanceCriteria.description: Attempt counter monotonic across N retries. Given a consumer that returns retry on every delivery, when the queue redelivers up to maxDeliveries, then each delivery carries an attempt count strictly greater than the previous (1, 2, 3, ...), and the counter does not reset mid-cycle; a mutation SIMULATE_ATTEMPT_RESET=true swaps two attempt values and the assertion FAILS.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a consumer that returns retry on every delivery
acceptanceCriteria.when: the queue redelivers up to maxDeliveries
acceptanceCriteria.then: each delivery carries a strictly greater attempt count; the reset mutation FAILS
